steps.title: Open the token page from Leafen
steps.caption: In Leafen, “Open Notion token page” opens Notion’s developer tools in a new tab.

steps.title: Create a connection
steps.caption: On app.notion.com/developers/connections (Developer connections in Notion’s developer tools), you click “New connection”.

steps.title: Name it and create it
steps.caption: You name it in “Connection name”, such as Leafen, keep “API token” and click “Create connection”.

steps.title: Choose the pages to move
steps.caption: In the connection’s “Content access”, you click “Edit access”, choose the top pages to move and click “Save”.

steps.title: Copy the API token
steps.caption: In “Configuration”, you check that “Read content” is ticked and copy the token (ntn_…) beside “API token”.

steps.title: Put the token into Leafen
steps.caption: Back in Leafen, you paste the token into the “Notion API token” field and click “Save token”.

steps.title: Choose what to move
steps.caption: You pick the pages and databases to move from what the connection reaches. A search finds deeper pages too.

screen.modalLead: A connection lets apps, agents and workflows log in to Notion. It can cover one workspace or several.
screen.apiTokenDesc: A fixed API token for one workspace, shared by collaborators, with its own access settings. It can’t go on Marketplace.
screen.oauthDesc: OAuth 2.0 per user, reaching only what the logged-in user can. It works across workspaces and can go on Marketplace.
screen.terms: Creating a connection means accepting Notion’s Developer Terms.
screen.contentAccessDesc: Pages and databases this connection can use
screen.pageAccessDesc: Set which pages this connection may reach. Unlinked pages can be added through search.
screen.tokenSectionDesc: API requests to this workspace authenticate with this token. Whoever holds it can act as this connection, so keep it secret.
screen.capabilitiesDesc: What this connection may do when called with its API token
screen.readContentDesc: View existing pages and database entries
